🔥🇲🇽 <u>Morena hauls Samuel García before anti-corruption prosecutors over 1.4 billion pesos</u>

Morena has filed a complaint with Nuevo León's anti-corruption prosecutor against Movimiento Ciudadano governor Samuel García, his wife Mariana Rodríguez and several relatives, alleging illicit enrichment, embezzlement and the triangulation of more than 1.4 billion pesos in public money through state suppliers into a tax-and-law firm tied to the governor's family. García brushed it off as a "refrito" — a rehash — and said "me río" ("I'm laughing"), even as the file lands months after a parallel complaint went to the federal FGR.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico laments Bachelet's exit from the UN race</u>

President Sheinbaum called Michelle Bachelet's withdrawal from the contest to lead the UN "lamentable," after Mexico and Brazil had backed the former Chilean president — who pulled out on Sept. 21 without the majority she needed in the Security Council's informal consultations. Bachelet, Sheinbaum said, "defends with her life the construction of peace, non-intervention, equality among states and multilateralism," the same principles Mexico says it will weigh before casting its next vote to succeed Guterres.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexico maps its own strategic minerals — for the nation, not the empire</u>

Mexico has finished exploring 13 strategic areas in Sonora and 19 more across seven states, with geological mapping now covering 56.6% of the territory (1.1 million km²) and 25 new prospective zones identified — including lithium at El Picacho and Sahuaripa under the state firm Litio para México, plus gold, silver, copper, zinc and even uranium and thorium anomalies, Contralínea reports. The point, the report argues, is to secure Mexico's own supply for the energy and tech transition instead of handing critical minerals to Washington under a modern "neocolonialism."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>1,640 hectares of Chapingo's forest seized by PRI-linked group</u>

Professors and students at the Universidad Autónoma Chapingo — Mexico's flagship agrarian university — say 1,640 hectares of their Zoquiapan experimental forest station in Ixtapaluca have been under seizure since October 2025 by ejidatarios and figures tied to the PRI-aligned Antorcha Campesina, who closed access, moved in heavy machinery and set up charcoal ovens and encampments. Among those the community names is México State's own agriculture secretary, María Eugenia Rojano Valdés, a Chapingo graduate.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Mexico probes Aeroméxico leak of 15 million passengers</u>

Mexico's Anti-Corruption and Good Government Ministry (SABG) has opened an investigation after a 1.10 GB database with the records of more than 15 million Aeroméxico customers — full names, emails, phones, birthdates — was put up for sale on Telegram. Officials pulled a sample of 100,092 records that included the data of public officials and figures, and traced the haul to an October 2025 international cyberattack rather than a fresh breach of the airline's systems.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>HOUSEHOLD SPENDING IS CARRYING MEXICO'S ECONOMY</u>

Household consumption drove almost all of Mexico's 1.1% GDP growth in the first half of 2026, contributing 1.5 of those points, per El Financiero's read of INEGI data — private consumption up 2.1% year-on-year and government consumption up 2.6%, even as productive investment barely moved at 0.3%. A year earlier that same investment line had subtracted 1.6 points; domestic demand, not foreign capital, is what is holding the floor.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>PAN MAYOR'S OFFICE FLAGGED FOR 31 MILLION PESOS IN GHOST CONTRACTS</u>

The federal auditor (ASF) referred former PAN borough chief Lía Limón to the FGR's anti-corruption unit over 31.49 million pesos in irregular 2022 contracts in Mexico City's Álvaro Obregón — public-lighting materials, uniforms and paint the borough could not prove were ever delivered. One vendor's registered address turned out to be an auto body shop; another, an empty apartment.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>MEXICAN FORCES FREE 3 MINERS, CAPTURE 7 SINALOA CARTEL GUNMEN</u>

In Puerto Peñasco, Sonora, the army and state investigators rescued three independent miners held captive and arrested seven alleged "Los Mayos" cartel members, seizing 40+ long guns, three machine guns, some 4,000 rounds and explosives. Three state agents were wounded but out of danger. Security chief Omar García Harfuch: "Their bravery, professionalism and commitment to protecting the population deserve all our respect."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>EX-BANXICO CHIEF ATTACKS THE 4T; THE NUMBERS BURY HIM</u>

When ex-Banxico governor Guillermo Ortiz attacked the government's record, Hacienda answered with data: poverty fell from 41.9% to 29.6% between 2018 and 2024 — more than 13 million people lifted out — with August inflation at 3.26%. Under Ortiz's own 1994–1997 tenure, patrimonial poverty jumped from 52.3% to 63.7%, food poverty from 21.2% to 33.3%, and inflation closed 1997 at 15.72%.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>DOS BOCAS KEEPS MEXICO'S DIESEL FLOWING AS WORLD PRICES SPIKE</u>

Sheinbaum: without the Olmeca refinery at Dos Bocas, "we'd be living a real problem." With international diesel prices climbing, Mexico is self-sufficient in diesel and holding gasoline and diesel prices steady through year's end via an IEPS subsidy. The rescue of Pemex and CFE — the same projects the opposition mocked — now covers 80% of the gasoline consumed in the country, with new coker plants in Tula and Salina Cruz coming online to lift low-sulfur output.
